The **ESC guidelines** (European Society of Cardiology guidelines) serve as the primary international professional reference for the clinical management of atrial fibrillation. Within the context of the Danish healthcare system's quality development programs, these guidelines are particularly significant for establishing the evidence-based foundation for structured [[patientuddannelse|Patientuddannelse]] (patient education) for individuals newly diagnosed with the condition [^src1]. 

The influence of the ESC guidelines on Danish clinical practice has evolved over recent years. In 2021, the ESC guidelines published by Hindricks et al. explicitly recommended patient education for atrial fibrillation patients and their relatives, which also helped form the basis for the integrated ABC Pathway treatment model [^src2]. Recognizing the growing importance of this intervention, the recent ESC guidelines gave higher weight to patient education, establishing the expectation that all patients with newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation should be offered structured training moving forward [^src1]. 

This international standard directly informs the development of [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], a national quality indicator that measures the proportion of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients who receive structured patient education within their first year of diagnosis [^src1]. To operationalize these international recommendations locally, a specific Danish guideline detailing the content of this education was developed in 2023, taking the ESC guidelines as its direct starting point [^src1]. Ultimately, the ESC guidelines anchor the broader narrative of systematic quality development in the Danish cardiovascular healthcare system, positioning patient-centered education as a core component of evidence-based practice.
